newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BARNES MAKES THE MOST OF BEASANT BLUNDER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARNES MAKES THE MOST OF BEASANT BLUNDER.

text.p: A blunder by Southampton goalkeeper Dave Beasant gifted Liverpool captain John Barnes a match-winning goal on his 300th league appearance for the club on Sunday.

With struggling Southampton having the better of a goalless stalemate against the premier league leaders, Beasant charged out to the right-hand side of his penalty area to clear an overhit through ball in the 76th minute.
He mishit his clearance to Barnes, who drilled a 40-metre shot into the empty net as Beasant made a desperate bid to make good his ground.

The 1-0 win carried Liverpool five points clear of their nearest challengers, champions Manchester United, Arsenal and Wimbledon. They have played 21 games, one more than United and Arsenal and two more than Wimbledon.
Beasant's gaffe was rough justice on a Southampton side who had carried more threat up front than their talented opposition in the second half.
Goalkeeper David James had to make three fine saves, one of them from a spectacular 30-metre volley from Matt le Tissier, during a five-minute spell midway through the half.
Liverpool central defender Mark Wright had come closest to breaking the deadlock in the first half when he headed on to the top of the Southampton bar with Beasant beaten.
Barnes was honest enough to admit that Liverpool were fortunate to win. "We were atrocious in the first half, not much better in the second and my goal was a bit of a fluke," he said.
Giving away soft goals has been Southampton's undoing so far this season, according to their manager Graeme Souness.
Souness, a former player and manager at Anfield, said: "We lost to them at Anfield through a soft goal in the 89th minute and we gave them an even dafter one today."
